meanings.primaryMeaning: Aadhya is a Sanskrit name meaning “first,” “primordial,” “original,” or “unrivaled excellence.”
meanings.traditionalInterpretation: Epithet of Goddess Durga/Shakti as the primordial divine power of the universe.
meanings.modernUsageNote: Popular modern Indian girl's personal name representing leadership and grace.

etymology.grammaticalNotes: Feminine form of ādya (first/initial) derived from ādi + yat suffix.

citations.translationEn: The primordial power (Ādyā Śakti) is the ultimate cause of all causes.
citations.verifiableNote: Attested epithet of the Divine Mother in Purāṇic literature.

meanings.primaryMeaning: Aarav is a Sanskrit-derived name meaning “peaceful,” “calm sound,” or “melodious resonance.”
meanings.traditionalInterpretation: In classical Sanskrit lexicons, ārava denotes a pleasant sound or musical resonance.
meanings.modernUsageNote: One of the most popular modern Indian names for boys, cherished for its peaceful aura.

etymology.grammaticalNotes: Prefix ā + root ru + ghañ suffix -> ārava (sound/resonance).

citations.verifiableNote: Sanskrit noun attested in classical lexicons; modernly used as a personal name symbolizing calm melody.

meanings.primaryMeaning: Abhimanyu is a Sanskrit name literally meaning “heroic,” “passionate,” “courageous,” or “possessing self-respect.”
meanings.literalSanskrit: Full of spirit, courage, or passion.
meanings.characterContext: Son of Arjuna and Subhadra, legendary young hero of the Kurukshetra war in the Mahabharata.
meanings.modernUsageNote: A classic heroic boy's personal name.

citations.translationEn: Mighty-armed Abhimanyu was a supreme warrior even in his youth.
citations.verifiableNote: Mahabharata Drona Parva recounts Abhimanyu's legendary valor in battle.

meanings.primaryMeaning: Acyuta is a Sanskrit name literally meaning “infallible,” “imperishable,” or “one who never falls.”
meanings.traditionalInterpretation: An epithet of Sri Krishna in Vishnu Sahasranama indicating unshakeable divine nature.
meanings.characterContext: Directly invoked by Arjuna in BG 1.21 to position his chariot between the armies.
meanings.modernUsageNote: A traditional, spiritual boy's personal name.

etymology.grammaticalNotes: Negation prefix a + past participle of root cyu.

citations.translationEn: O Infallible One (Acyuta), please draw my chariot up between the two armies.
citations.verifiableNote: Arjuna invokes Krishna as Acyuta in Chapter 1 of the Gita.

meanings.primaryMeaning: Aditi is a Vedic Sanskrit name meaning “boundless,” “unbroken,” “freedom,” or “infinite cosmic expansion.”
meanings.traditionalInterpretation: The Vedic Mother of the Devas (Adityas) representing the boundless universe and creative nature.
meanings.modernUsageNote: A beloved, timeless girl's name symbolizing cosmic grace and freedom.

citations.sanskritSnippetSa: अदितिर्द्यौरदितिरन्तरिक्षम् अदितिर्माता स पिता स पुत्रः।
citations.translationEn: Aditi is the sky, Aditi is the atmosphere, Aditi is the mother, father, and son...
citations.verifiableNote: Famous Vedic hymn celebrating Aditi as cosmic infinity.

meanings.primaryMeaning: Aditya means “son of Aditi,” “sun deity,” “radiant solar deity,” or “luminous light.”
meanings.traditionalInterpretation: The Sun God who illuminates the worlds and dispels darkness.
meanings.characterContext: Invoked in Gita 10.21 where Krishna states 'Among the Adityas, I am Vishnu.'
meanings.modernUsageNote: One of the most classic and widely chosen names for boys in India.

citations.translationEn: Among the Adityas, I am Vishnu.
citations.verifiableNote: Krishna explicitly cites Aditya in Chapter 10 of the Gita.

meanings.primaryMeaning: Arjuna is a Sanskrit name literally meaning “bright,” “white,” “clear,” or “silver.”
meanings.traditionalInterpretation: One whose deeds are untarnished and pure (Shukla-karma).
meanings.characterContext: The third Pandava prince in the Mahabharata and recipient of Sri Krishna’s divine wisdom in the Bhagavad Gita.
meanings.modernUsageNote: A timeless Indian boy’s personal name associated with focus, archery mastery, and righteousness.

etymology.rootMeaning: to shine, earn, acquire, or be bright
etymology.grammaticalNotes: Derived from Sanskrit root arj + Unadi suffix un.

citations.sanskritSnippetSa: पृथिव्यां चतुरन्तायां वर्णो मे दुर्लभो समः। करोमि कर्म शुक्लानि तेनाहमर्जुनो स्मृतः॥
citations.translationEn: My skin is clear and bright, and my deeds are untarnished; hence I am remembered as Arjuna.
citations.verifiableNote: Arjuna explicitly explains his name's literal meaning ('bright/untarnished') to Prince Uttara in the Virata Parva.

citations.translationEn: Your right is to work only, but never to its fruits.
citations.verifiableNote: Arjuna is the direct recipient of Krishna's battlefield discourse in all 18 chapters of the Gita.

meanings.primaryMeaning: Chanakya is an ancient Indian personal name meaning “son of Chānaka,” “master strategist,” or “renowned scholar.”
meanings.traditionalInterpretation: Symbol of supreme political wisdom, statecraft, and intellectual mastery.
meanings.characterContext: Master strategist and prime minister of Chandragupta Maurya who established the Mauryan Empire.
meanings.modernUsageNote: A distinguished Indian boy's personal name associated with wisdom and leadership.

etymology.grammaticalNotes: Patronymic derivative formed with yañ suffix.

citations.translationEn: Kautilya (Chanakya) will uproot the nine Nandas and establish Chandragupta.
citations.verifiableNote: Purāṇic text recording Chanakya establishing the Mauryan dynasty.

meanings.primaryMeaning: Krishna is a Sanskrit name literally meaning “dark,” “dark-blue,” or “the all-attractive one.”
meanings.traditionalInterpretation: The Supreme Personality whose divine beauty attracts all living beings.
meanings.characterContext: The Eighth Avatar of Vishnu, central guide of the Mahabharata, and speaker of the Bhagavad Gita.
meanings.modernUsageNote: One of the most revered and widely used personal names across India and globally.

citations.sanskritSnippetSa: कृषिर भू-वाचकः शब्दो णश् च निर्वृति-वाचकः। तयोः समैक्यं परं ब्रह्म कृष्ण इत्य् अभिधीयते॥
citations.translationEn: The root 'kṛṣ' denotes attraction/existence, and 'ṇa' denotes eternal bliss; their union is known as Krishna.
citations.verifiableNote: Mahabharata Udyoga Parva explicitly provides this etymological definition.

meanings.primaryMeaning: Rama is a Sanskrit name literally meaning “pleasing,” “charming,” “delightful,” or “one who brings joy.”
meanings.traditionalInterpretation: One in whom the sages delight (Ramante yogino 'nante).
meanings.characterContext: Hero of the Ramayana and Seventh Avatar of Vishnu, referenced in Bhagavad Gita 10.31.
meanings.modernUsageNote: A deeply honored personal name in Indian culture.

etymology.rootMeaning: to delight, rejoice, or rest in
etymology.grammaticalNotes: Derived from root ram + ghañ suffix.

citations.translationEn: Among wielders of weapons, I am Rama.
citations.verifiableNote: Bhagavad Gita 10.31 explicitly names Rama among divine opulences.

meanings.primaryMeaning: Tanay is a modern Indian boy's name derived from the classical Sanskrit word Tanaya (तनय), meaning “son,” “offspring,” or “continuation of the family lineage.”
meanings.literalSanskrit: Born of oneself; extending the family lineage.
meanings.traditionalInterpretation: In classical Sanskrit, tanaya refers to a son who extends the family line.
meanings.modernUsageNote: Tanay is a modern personal name form resulting from Hindi/vernacular schwa-deletion of the classical Sanskrit noun tanaya.

etymology.rootMeaning: to extend, stretch out, or continue
etymology.grammaticalNotes: Derived from root tan + suffix as/aya -> Tanaya (masculine noun: son; feminine Tanayā: daughter).

citations.verifiableNote: Rigveda 1.92.13 attests the common noun tanaya ('offspring/child'), not an ancient hero or personal name called Tanay.

meanings.primaryMeaning: Vedant is a Sanskrit name meaning “pinnacle of Vedic wisdom,” “end of the Vedas,” or “ultimate spiritual truth.”
meanings.traditionalInterpretation: The Upanishadic philosophy representing the ultimate goal of Vedic wisdom.
meanings.characterContext: Invoked in Gita 15.15 where Krishna states 'I am the author of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.'
meanings.modernUsageNote: A very popular modern Indian boy's name.

citations.translationEn: I am the compiler of Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.
citations.verifiableNote: Krishna explicitly identifies himself as the author of Vedanta in BG 15.15.
